raised.claim: A non-empty beer_ids list makes a review_class-only where legal, and that where still accepts every later row of the class.
raised.why_it_breaks: Model submits scope {beer_ids:[7], where:[{col:'review_class', op:'=', value:'matcher_bug'}]}. isLegalScope returns true immediately, so guard 1 does not drop it. rowSatisfiesScope only short-circuits beer 7; any other matcher_bug verdict matches the where (verdict class equals 'matcher_bug') and is attached. That is the #347 whole-class magnet, with one enumerated id as a bypass.

raised.claim: Verdicts filed against a new issue are never checked against that issue's scope, so a contradicting row is linked on creation day and never rechecked.
raised.why_it_breaks: new_issues scope is {beer_ids:[], where:[{col:'candidates_count', op:'=', value:0}]} and the only verdict is beer 1 with candidates_count 5 and new_issue_key set. isLegalScope passes, the else branch attaches the verdict, and the job writes issue_number. The row now has review_class set, so it leaves the untriaged pool and guard 2 never sees it.

raised.claim: Saturation is checked against the pre-run count only, so one run can attach a full batch past MAX_ROWS_PER_ISSUE.
raised.why_it_breaks: An open issue has postCreationRows 0 (or 11). The model returns 40 in-batch verdicts all pointing at that issue number. Each comparison still sees 0 (or 11), all 40 are pushed into one comment, and the issue jumps to 40 (or 51) rows before the next run's count can refuse further attachments.

raised.claim: The model-authored issue body is placed before the scope fence, and parseScopeBlock keeps the first ```triage-scope block, so model prose can replace the real scope.
raised.why_it_breaks: Open-issue bodies in the prompt already contain ```triage-scope fences. The model copies one into new_issue.body, for example a valid {"beer_ids":[999],"where":[]} block, and the job appends the real block after it. Next run BLOCK_RE.exec returns the copied block, not the rendered one, and attachments are accepted or rejected against a scope nobody stored in the structured field. A copied fence that is not valid JSON makes parseScopeBlock return null, so the issue accepts nothing.

raised.claim: guardHits are logged only when some orphan has no verdict, so a full batch of guard-rejected verdicts never emits the shortfall line.
raised.why_it_breaks: The model returns one verdict per orphan, all pointing at an illegal scope or a scope the rows contradict. covered counts those beer_ids before the guards, so covered === orphans.length, the warn is skipped, and plan.guardHits is not in the finish() outcome either. The rows stay review_class NULL and return tomorrow with no per-guard counter in the log.

raised.claim: Absence is treated as proved when either probe field is empty, even if the other field returned hits.
raised.why_it_breaks: Probe for beer 1 is {brewery:'', name:'Mad Elf'}. proved is true because brewery === '', so a not_on_untappd verdict is kept and written as terminal. The name probe found a beer, which is the brewery-label case the prompt says is not absence; the row is closed instead of degraded to matcher_bug.

raised.claim: Guard 3's degraded matcher_bug quiet verdicts are counted as wontfix in the digest.
raised.why_it_breaks: A run with no search dep degrades not_on_untappd to matcher_bug and pushes it onto plan.quiet. The else branch increments outcome.wontfix, so buildTriageLine reports wontfix even though the row was stored as matcher_bug and remains in the enrichment pool.

raised.quote:
review_class       = CASE
         WHEN (enrich_failures.candidates_count = 0) <> (excluded.candidates_count = 0)
         THEN NULL ELSE enrich_failures.review_class END,
       review_note        = CASE
         WHEN (enrich_failures.candidates_count = 0) <> (excluded.candidates_count = 0)
         THEN NULL ELSE enrich_failures.review_note END,
       reviewed_at        = CASE
         WHEN (enrich_failures.candidates_count = 0) <> (excluded.candidates_count = 0)
         THEN NULL ELSE enrich_failures.reviewed_at END`,
raised.claim: Reopening a failure when candidates_count crosses 0 clears the review fields but leaves the new issue_number column set.
raised.why_it_breaks: A row linked to issue 347 later fails again with candidates_count crossing 0. review_class and reviewed_at become NULL so it re-enters triage, but issue_number stays 347. Any query that treats issue_number as the authoritative link still counts it as attached, and countRowsForIssue undercounts it only because reviewed_at is NULL, so the saturation slot is freed while the stale link remains.

raised.claim: The load-bearing triage-scope block is appended after the model body, so the 2000-character prompt cap can hide it from the model.
raised.why_it_breaks: A created issue whose prose body is longer than ISSUE_BODY_CAP (2000) has the scope fence past the slice. The next prompt shows the issue with no scope, the model attaches a contradicting row, and guard 2 skips it. The row stays untriaged and the model cannot see the necessary condition it failed.
